question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral
$\displaystyle \int_{0}^{π/4}10\cdot \frac{\sec x\tan x}{1 + \sec x}dx$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\sec{\left(x \right)} + 1.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\tan{\left(x \right)} \sec{\left(x \right)}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\tan{\left(x \right)} \sec{\left(x \right)}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi}{4}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $1 + \sqrt{2}$ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{10 \tan{\left(x \right)} \sec{\left(x \right)}}{\sec{\left(x \right)} + 1}\,\text{d}x &= \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{1}{\sec{\left(x \right)} + 1}\cdot (10 \tan{\left(x \right)} \sec{\left(x \right)})\,\text{d}x \\ &= \int_{2}^{1 + \sqrt{2}}\frac{1}{u}\cdot 10\,\text{d}u \\ &= 10\ln|u|\big|_{2}^{1 + \sqrt{2}} \\ &= 10\left(\ln(1 + \sqrt{2})-\ln(2)\right) \\ &= 10\left(- \ln{\left(2 \right)} + \ln{\left(1 + \sqrt{2} \right)}\right)\end{aligned}
$$
